item.title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
item.content:encoded: Identity alone doesn't guarantee a bot will behave responsibly. We are introducing a system to continuously evaluate whether Verified bots honor site preferences, like robots.txt and HTTP 429s, ensuring they remain accountable over time.

item.title: A fully programmable secure web gateway
item.content:encoded: Cloudflare Gateway and Data Loss Prevention have inherited the flexibility and power of Cloudflare Workers through our full-stack integration with the Cloudflare Developer platform.

item.title: Deploy with Void
item.content:encoded: Introducing Void: an open-source SDK, CLI, and self-hosted platform for building full-stack Vite apps and deploying them to Cloudflare.

item.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyone
item.content:encoded: How Cloudflare and OpenAI are working together to help AI find useful content, keep up with changes, and make fewer wasted requests — making the experience better for users and website owners alike.

item.title: Yandex outage: Data shows that instead of going dark, malicious bots went on the move
item.content:encoded: When strikes hit Yandex data centers, many assumed Russian bot operations went dark. Cloudflare data reveals that while search crawling stopped, malicious bots simply migrated to other networks.

item.title: Inside Hyperdrive: How we solved a rare Hyperdrive MySQL caching bug
item.content:encoded: While adding MySQL support to Hyperdrive, we found a subtle protocol bug when caching query results. Here is how we tracked down a 0.001% rate error and made Hyperdrive MySQL generally available.

item.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
item.content:encoded: A deep dive into how D1 architected its control plane to scale and manage millions of databases, while keeping data plane query operations at the edge. We share guiding principles on how to build on the Developer Platform effectively.

item.title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
item.content:encoded: Our strategies to optimize our data pipeline throughput without compromising data quality.

item.title: Filter, reshape, and redact logs before export with Transformers
item.content:encoded: Logpush now supports Transformers, allowing teams to filter, redact, and reshape log streams using SQL before export. Powered by Apache DataFusion and Apache Arrow, Transformers apply those changes directly to log data before it reaches the destination.

item.title: Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash
item.content:encoded: We are expanding the Clef decision model family with Clef-omni, natively processing audio, video, images, and text in a single pipeline. We’ve also lowered Clef-flash pricing and boosted Clef inference speeds by up to 2.0x.

item.title: Introducing on-demand CPU and memory profiling with flamegraphs for Workers and Durable Objects
item.content:encoded: On-demand CPU and memory profiling for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects is now available. Now you can generate interactive flamegraphs directly in production to quickly track down memory leaks and performance bottlenecks.

item.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
item.content:encoded: The Deno team is joining Cloudflare to radically simplify self-hosting Workers and Durable Objects, so developers can use the same primitives in more places.

item.title: Bridging technical depth and usability: The story behind Radar’s redesign
item.content:encoded: We redesigned Cloudflare Radar to make real-time global traffic and outage data accessible to a wider audience — including journalists, less technical researchers, and everyday users. By introducing an interactive map and standardized components, we simplified navigation while preserving technical depth.

item.title: Building an evidence-grounded agentic security operations harness on Cloudflare
item.content:encoded: Cloudflare Managed Defense uses a team of specialized AI agents built on Workers and global network telemetry to analyze security alerts. By separating deterministic evidence collection from model inference, the system delivers grounded recommendations to Managed Defense Analysts.

item.title: The keys to the Internet change on October 11. Are you ready?
item.content:encoded: On October 11, 2026, the DNS root switches to a new key-signing key (KSK-2024). Learn what this means for you, and how RFC 8509 trust anchor sentinels allow you to test whether your DNS resolver is ready for the rollover.

item.title: Everything we launched during Birthday Week 2026
item.content:encoded: We celebrated our 16th birthday with 46 announcements across open source, post-quantum security, AI agents, and developer platform upgrades. Here’s a day-by-day roundup of everything we shipped.

item.title: One year later: the power of 1.1.1.1 interns
item.content:encoded: A year after announcing our goal to hire 1,111 interns, more than 750 early-career builders have shipped real products across 48 teams at Cloudflare. From Birthday Week launches to post-quantum security, our interns prove that AI amplifies human potential instead of replacing it.

item.title: 8 major updates to Cloudflare Observability
item.content:encoded: Cloudflare is launching eight major updates that bring logs, traces, analytics, alerts, dashboards, querying, and telemetry export into one observability platform, with simpler and more predictable pricing.

item.title: Streamline: custom video pipelines with Cloudflare Stream and Workers
item.content:encoded: Streamline demonstrates how to build long-running, continuous video processing pipelines by pairing Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects with a containerized media engine.

item.title: Introducing Web Search API via AI Gateway
item.content:encoded: Cloudflare AI Gateway now supports native web search API integration in partnership with Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. Developers can now inject real-time web context into model inference calls via AI Gateway, REST APIs, or Workers bindings.
